messages:
maya: quick check — incoming customer security questionnaire asks whether our logs can contain customer PII (emails, account ids) and how logs are encrypted + subprocessors. Need a short, audit-ready answer + links. pinging @tom @priya @owen @jenna

tom: short answer: we do not persist raw email addresses in app logs. Ingest pipeline redacts/hashs sensitive fields; we keep only surrogate ids and domain parts for routing. logs may contain internal user_id (not the customer's external id).

priya: adding a little detail we usually provide in Qs: redaction happens at the logging ingestion layer (sidecar/ingest lambda) using a salted one-way hash for emails and phone numbers. we also mask JSON fields like `credit_card_number` and `ssn`. example regex/logic we use:
```
# pseudocode
if field looks_like_email(value):
  value = hash_with_kms_salt(value)
else if matches_sensitive_pattern(value):
  value = mask(value)
```

owen: storage detail for the Q: logs are written to S3 with SSE-KMS (key alias `alias/redwood-logs-prod`) and bucket policies restrict access to the logging-processor role. retention lifecycle = 90 days (archive then delete). For Dedicated/Private customers we can keep logs in their VPC/S3 per contract — mention that as an option.

jenna: for the customer answer we should be explicit and conservative. Proposed bullet text I can use for the questionnaire: 
- We do not intentionally store customer PII in application logs.
- A logging ingestion pipeline redacts and/or one-way hashes sensitive fields prior to persistence. Hash salts/keys are managed in KMS.
- Logs at rest are encrypted using AWS SSE-KMS; access is limited via IAM and audited.
- Subprocessors include AWS (S3), Datadog (metrics/structured events), and Google BigQuery (aggregates). Full raw request payloads are not forwarded to third-party processors.
- Retention: 90 days (configurable for Dedicated/Private).
Can someone confirm Datadog forwarding semantics? do we ever send raw payloads there?

maya: we only send structured events and metrics to Datadog; no raw request bodies. we do forward anonymized traces (span ids) for troubleshooting.

sec-bot: evidence added to SOC2 tracker: https://redwood.internal/docs/soc2/logging-evidence (audit id: 2026-LOG-03). Also uploaded: ingest-redaction-snippet.txt and kms-key-policy.pdf.

owen: small addition — mention that the ingest pipeline keeps a short-term plaintext buffer (in-memory / ephemeral) for parsing, but nothing is persisted unredacted. That helped in previous customer reviews, be transparent about it.

tom: suggested final wording (concise, customer-friendly):
"We do not store customer PII in application logs. Our ingestion pipeline performs one-way hashing and masking of sensitive fields before data is persisted; hashing keys are managed in AWS KMS. Logs at rest are encrypted with SSE-KMS and access is restricted by IAM. Subprocessors used for logging/analytics include AWS (S3), Datadog (metrics/structured events only), and Google BigQuery (aggregates). Retention is 90 days by default; Dedicated/Private customers may configure longer retention in their environment. See internal evidence: https://redwood.internal/docs/soc2/logging-evidence (2026-LOG-03)."

priya: :thumbsup: small language nit — replace "one-way hashing" with "one-way hashing with salts managed in KMS" (legal likes that).

jenna: approved with that edit. I'll paste this into the questionnaire and send.

maya: thanks everyone — I'll submit the response and attach the SOC2 evidence. Closing thread.
